proposals.before: Dou Tai, styled Shining Tranquility, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
proposals.after: Dou Tai, courtesy name Shining, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
proposals.reason: 「世寧」is a courtesy name; 'Shining Tranquility' invents a gloss not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Dou Tai, styled Shining Tranquility, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
proposals.after: Dou Tai, courtesy name Shining, was a native of Da'an Hanshu.
proposals.reason: Same courtesy-name mistranslation as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: He rose to three imperators' protocol of the open office.
proposals.reason: 「儀同三司」is garbled as 'three imperators' protocol'; standard rendering is Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes.

proposals.before: He rose to three imperators' protocol of the open office.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: As Wucheng sickened toward death, he entrusted the final testament to Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others alike — and made Dingyuan minister of works.
proposals.after: As Wucheng grew gravely ill, Dingyuan together with the Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui and others received the final testament; Dingyuan was made minister of works.
proposals.reason: Chinese subject of 與…同受顧命 is Dingyuan (continuing prior sentence), not Wucheng entrusting to Rui alone; idiomatic reverses the recipient structure.

proposals.before: Soon he was removed and made Governor of Ying Province.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed Governor of Ying Province.
proposals.reason: 「除」here means appoint to office, not 'removed'; the idiomatic correctly has 'made governor'.

proposals.before: Once at the capital, Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou carried on with excessive ribaldry at court — and none of the nobles dared rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed; men praised Gan for it.
proposals.after: Once at the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei, carried on with excessive ribaldry at court — and none of the nobles dared rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him. Xiaoyou was deeply shamed; men praised Gan for it.
proposals.reason: English fuses the title and personal name as 'Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou'; Chinese 魏譙王元孝友 is Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei.

proposals.before: Once when he visited the capital, Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou indulged in excessive ribaldry at court — none of the nobles could rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him; Xiaoyou was deeply ashamed, and contemporaries praised Gan.
proposals.after: Once when he visited the capital, Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei, indulged in excessive ribaldry at court — none of the nobles could rebuke him to his face. Gan sternly reproached him; Xiaoyou was deeply ashamed, and contemporaries praised Gan.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise fuses title and name; reorder to match 魏譙王元孝友.

proposals.before: Earlier, Dingyuan's brother Jilue had a performing concubine. Mutipo demanded her; Dingyuan refused.
proposals.after: Earlier, Dingyuan's younger brother Jilue had a performing concubine. Mutipo demanded her; Dingyuan refused.
proposals.reason: Chinese 弟 marks younger brother; idiomatic omits the relative-age sense present in the literal.

proposals.before: Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful. After Qi's fall she was given to Duke of Xue Changsun Lan.
proposals.after: Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful. After Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue.
proposals.reason: 薛公長孫覽 is Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue; English fuses the fief title as if Xue were the surname.

proposals.before: Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Duke of Xue Changsun Lan.
proposals.after: Shiwen's cousin had been a concubine of Qi — beautiful; after Qi's fall she was given to Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue.
proposals.reason: Same name-order error: 長孫覽 is the personal name and 薛公 the ducal title.

proposals.before: Later, when Tang Junming, governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
proposals.after: Later, when Tang Junming, governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, he took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
proposals.reason: Chinese 娉以為妻 continues 唐君明 as subject; Shiwen did not marry her.

proposals.before: Later, when Tang Junming, Governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, Shiwen took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
proposals.after: Later, when Tang Junming, Governor of Ying Province, was in mourning for his mother, he took her as his wife — for this both Junming and Shiwen were impeached by the censorate.
proposals.reason: Same reversed-subject error: 娉以為妻 refers to Tang Junming marrying the cousin during mourning.

proposals.before: When Gao Yang succeeded to power, he held the Heyang garrison and routed Western general Yang Piao and others.
proposals.after: When Gao Yang succeeded to power, Le held the Heyang garrison and routed Western general Yang Piao and others.
proposals.reason: Chinese silent subject of 鎮河陽 and 破西將 is the biographical subject Pan Le, not Gao Yang; the idiomatic 'he' after 'When Gao Yang succeeded' wrongly attributes the garrison and victory to Gao Yang.

proposals.before: When Wenxuan succeeded to affairs, he garrisoned Heyang and defeated Western generals Yang Piao and others.
proposals.after: When Wenxuan succeeded to affairs, Le garrisoned Heyang and defeated Western generals Yang Piao and others.
proposals.reason: Chinese silent subject of 鎮河陽 and 破西將 is Pan Le; literal 'he' after Wenxuan wrongly makes Wenxuan the garrison commander.

proposals.before: In the sixth year of Tianbao he died at Xuanchi.
proposals.after: In the sixth year of Tianbao he died at Xuanhu.
proposals.reason: 懸瓠 is the place-name Xuanhu (hú), not Xuanchi; the idiomatic rendering corrupts the toponym.

proposals.before: In the sixth year of Tianbao, he died at Xuanchi.
proposals.after: In the sixth year of Tianbao, he died at Xuanhu.
proposals.reason: 懸瓠 romanizes as Xuanhu; Xuanchi is a clear mistranslation of 瓠.

decisions.reason: 字世寧 is a courtesy name; “Shining Tranquility” invents a semantic gloss absent from the Chinese, while courtesy name Shining restores the romanized 字.
Literal likewise invents “Shining Tranquility” for 世寧; courtesy name Shining matches the 字 without the false gloss.
位儀同三司 is the office Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes; “three imperators’ protocol of the open office” is a garbled mistranslation with no basis in the Chinese.
Literal repeats the same garble of 儀同三司; Equal-to-the-Three-Dukes correctly names the office.
Preceding units concern 定遠; 與趙郡王等同受顧命 makes Dingyuan a co-recipient of the dying charge with the Prince of Zhao, not Wucheng entrusting the testament to Rui alone.
尋除瀛州刺史 uses 除 in the appointment sense; “removed and made” invents a dismissal absent from the Chinese.
魏譙王元孝友 is Yuan Xiaoyou holding the title Prince Qiao of Wei; fusing them as “Prince Qiao of Wei Yuan Xiaoyou” muddles title and personal name.
Literal has the same title–name fusion; reordering to Yuan Xiaoyou, Prince Qiao of Wei matches 魏譙王元孝友.
定遠弟季略 uses 弟 for younger brother; adding “younger” restores the kinship marked in the Chinese without other change.
薛公長孫覽 is Changsun Lan with the ducal title Duke of Xue; “Duke of Xue Changsun Lan” wrongly suggests Xue as a surname element.
Literal likewise fuses 薛公 with 長孫覽; Changsun Lan, Duke of Xue correctly separates personal name and title.
唐君明居母憂，娉以為妻 continues Junming as subject of 娉以為妻; Shiwen did not take her as wife, though both were later impeached.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唐君明居母憂，娉以為妻

decisions.reason: Literal repeats the reversed subject; 娉以為妻 refers to Tang Junming marrying during mourning, not Shiwen.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 唐君明居母憂，娉以為妻

decisions.reason: 文宣嗣事 is a temporal frame; the silent subject of 鎮河陽 and 破西將 is biographical Pan Le, confirmed by later 還鎮河陽 with 樂 as subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 文宣嗣事，鎮河陽，破西將楊檦等

decisions.reason: Literal’s “he” after Wenxuan wrongly makes the emperor garrison Heyang; silent subject of 鎮河陽/破西將 is Le.
懸瓠 is the place-name Xuanhu (瓠 = hú); Xuanchi misreads the second character.
Literal likewise has Xuanchi for 懸瓠; Xuanhu restores the correct toponym.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Shining Tranquility came only from inventing a gloss of 世寧; the courtesy-name claim must read Shining while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
